name: fmt
one_liner: A super-fast, safe way for software to turn numbers and data into readable text — the plumbing behind countless apps' log messages and output, invisible to end users.
buyer: Not really a buyer situation — this is infrastructure that C++ engineering teams adopt for free to make their own software faster and safer, not something anyone pays for directly.
business_use_cases: A game studio uses it to format debug logs and in-game text fast enough not to hurt frame rate.
A trading firm's C++ engine uses it for low-latency logging where iostream would be too slow.
An embedded-systems team uses it to keep compiled code size small on constrained hardware.

money_ideas.idea: No direct monetization path for an outside operator — the value only shows up inside someone else's product.

steal_this: There isn't a weekend product here; if anything, offer paid C++ performance-audit consulting to teams still using slow iostream/printf and show them the before/after numbers.
